title: Short-lived high-volume Bernoulli bandits with bounded-density priors
summary: Long-run Bayesian average loss with random arriving arms, finite lifetimes, and entire-round batched feedback.

description_paragraphs: Minimize long-run Bayesian average loss relative to the best currently alive arm in a streaming short-lived high-volume bandit.
task.formulation: Minimize long-run Bayesian average loss relative to the best currently alive arm in a streaming short-lived high-volume bandit.

description_paragraphs: At the start of every calendar round t, a new disjoint cohort A_t of k arms arrives. An arm born at t remains available through t+w inclusive. Thus there are w+1 alive cohorts after initialization and w useful feedback opportunities before its last allocation.

Each arm mean is drawn independently from a distribution D on [0,1]. Conditional on all means, rewards are independent Bernoulli draws across arms and plays. The prior density satisfies $c_1\le f(u)\le c_2$ almost everywhere, where $0<c_1\le1\le c_2<\infty$. Arrival identities and times contain no mean information. The parameters w,c_1,c_2 are fixed for the rate statements.

description_paragraphs: At each round the policy chooses nonnegative integer allocations $\pi_t(a)$ to alive arms, with $\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\pi_t(a)=n$. The entire allocation is measurable before any reward from that round is revealed. All rewards from these n plays are revealed together afterward; no within-round adaptation or stopping is permitted.

The values n,k,w,c_1,c_2 are public. The policy may be given D; the upper policy uses only its density bounds, and the lower bound holds even when D is the known uniform prior. The arm means are hidden.

description_paragraphs: Let $\mu_t^*=\max_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\mu_a$. For a finite evaluation horizon T, $\mathcal L_{n,T}(\pi;D)=(nT)^{-1}\mathbb E_D\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\pi_t(a)(\mu_t^*-\mu_a)$. The expectation includes the prior, rewards, and policy randomness.

The long-run risk uses $\overline{\mathcal L}_n(\pi;D)=\limsup_{T\to\infty}\mathcal L_{n,T}(\pi;D)$. Define $\mathcal L_n^*(c_1,c_2)=\inf_\pi\sup_{D\in\mathfrak D(c_1,c_2)}\overline{\mathcal L}_n(\pi;D)$, allowing a policy to take D as input. The expectation precedes the limit superior; this is not an expectation-of-limsup criterion.

description_paragraphs: The resource parameters are n plays per calendar round, k arriving arms per round, and lifetime w+1 rounds. There are nT rewards over a finite T-round evaluation. The asymptotic rate sends n to infinity at fixed w,c_1,c_2, with k possibly depending on n; T is sent to infinity inside the long-run performance criterion.

description_paragraphs: All randomized policies with allocations measurable before current-round feedback are allowed. Arms may be sampled multiple times in a round, but allocations cannot adapt within that round. The prior may be known.

One upper policy depending only on n,k,w,c_1,c_2 handles every density in the class. The lower bound holds for every policy under the fixed known uniform prior and even for liminf of the finite-horizon expected losses.

regimes.name: Finite lifetime with arbitrary arrival count
regimes.predicate_text: Fix integer $w\ge1$ and $0<c_1\le1\le c_2<\infty$; require $n\ge n_0(w,c_1,c_2)$ and any integer $k\ge1$. No ambient Euclidean dimension; the number of alive arms is at most k(w+1). The lower bound is for liminf of expected averages, hence also bounds the same limsup-risk used by the upper bound.
